``` text
📁 STAT118/

   └── 📁 images/
```

### R and Rstudio

#### What is the difference?

R is the engine and RStudio is the car. 

#### What do the different windows do?

The **Source** window is where you will create and edit your Quarto documents, and write your code. This window should be in the top left pane.

The **Console** window is where the code is run. This window should be in the top right pane.

The **Environment** window will show you the objects and other things that you have created and defined in your code. this should be on the bottom left. 

The window on the lower right should include **Files, Plots, Packages, Help, and Viewer** (it's ok if there are additional tabs). This is where you can look for help documentation on the different functions available through R and additional R packages. This is also where figures and rendered files should pop up. 

### Settings

#### Rearrange panes

If your panes are not in the configuration outlined above, please change them using the instructions below. 

Go to:

`Tools → Global Options → Pane Layout`

#### Change theme

If you want to change how your RStudio appears.

We decided that I could continue to use my dark theme. Yay!

Go to:

`Tools → Global Options → Appearance`


#### Change Downloads Permission

Please take a minute to change your downloads permissions for the browser that you use. This will make it easier for you to direct downloads to the correct folder and not have to go hunting for things that got sent to weird places. 

**Google Chrome:**

1.  Go to the three-dot menu (top-right corner) → Settings.

2.  Scroll down and click Downloads.

3.  Toggle on “Ask where to save each file before downloading.”

**Firefox:**

1.  Click the three-line menu (top-right corner) → Settings.

2.  In the General section, under Files and Applications, select: “Always ask you where to save files.”

**Safari (Mac):**

1.  Go to Safari \> Preferences \> General.

2.  Under File download location, select: “Ask for each download.”

### Quarto

#### Source vs. Visual

#### Markdown Syntax

##### Bold and Italics

You make **bold** text by placing two `*` before and after the text you wish to **bold**: `**make this text bold**`

**make this text bold**

You make *italics* text by placing one `*` before and after the text you wish to appear in *italics*: `*make this text italics*`

*make this text italics*

You make ***bold and italics*** text by placing three `*` before and after the text you wish to appear in ***bold and italics***: `***make this text bold and italics***`

***make this text bold and italics***

##### Lists

To make a list put a `-` before each item on the list. 

```
a list

-   one thing
-   second thing
-   third thing

```

The result will look like this:

a list

-   one thing
-   second thing
-   third thing

*Always make sure to include an empty line before the first item on the list, otherwise it will not render properly.*

##### Hyperlink

To add a hyperlink use this syntax:

`[words here](link here)`

The text should look like this:

`[this is a link to the class website](https://cschine.github.io/my_class_website/courses/STAT118/)`

The result will look like this:

[this is a link to the class website](https://cschine.github.io/my_class_website/courses/STAT118/)


##### Images

To add an image, use this syntax:

`![caption](image)`

The text should look something like this:

`![this is an image](images/NBP_midnight_sun.jpeg)`

And the result will look like this:

![this is an image](images/NBP_midnight_sun.jpeg){width=70%}

#### Using R in Quarto

R code chunks

Use the green +C buttom in the toolbar to add a code chunk

```{r}



```


Create an object like this:

```{r}

aardvark <- 17

yeti <- 23

```


You can do basic arithmetic with named objects using the standard operators:

| Operator    | Description    |
|-------------|----------------|
| `+`         | Addition       |
| `-`         | Subtraction    |
| `*`         | Multiplication |
| `/`         | Division       |
| `^` or `**` | Exponentiation |

Like this:

```{r}

aardvark*yeti

aardvark/yeti

chalk <- aardvark*yeti

chalk

```

To comment code use the `#` at the beginning of the line and write a description of what the code should be doing, or a note to yourself, or whatever you want. Like this: 

```{r}
# multiply aardvark and yeti
aardvark*yeti

# divide aardvark by yeti
aardvark/yeti

# assign chalk a value of aardvark multiplied by yeti
chalk <- aardvark*yeti

# call chalk up
chalk
```

#### Render

Now it is time to Render your Quarto (.qmd) doc into a .html file (which is the format in which you will be submitting all of your assignments). To do this press the ![render arrow](images/Render.png) Render button, which should be visible in the toolbar at the top of your Source Pane (the pane in which you are editing your Quarto document).

If your quarto doc does not render correctly, errors can be found in the Background Jobs tab in the Console Pane. This can be very useful and sometimes very confusing.
